options.title: Colgan Air: Why Didn't the Stick Pusher Save It?
options.first_line: Colgan Air's airliner had a machine built to shove its nose down out of a stall. Why didn't it work?
options.first_frame: a blueprint cutaway of the airliner's cockpit at night, the control column sliding forward on its own under a mono PUSHER ACTIVE label, the date caption and the reconstruction tag

options.title: Colgan Air: The Plane Pushed the Nose Down. Someone Pulled It Back.
options.first_line: At {fact7} knots near Buffalo, Colgan Air's airliner started pushing its own nose down.
options.first_frame: the twin-propeller airliner in 3D side-on over the snowy cloud, its nose dipping by itself, the airspeed box beside it reading the figure, the reconstruction tag

options.title: The Machine That Tried to Save Colgan Air Flight 3407
options.first_line: Colgan Air's flight to Buffalo had a hidden safety machine, and that night it fired three times.
options.first_frame: a blueprint X-ray of the cockpit floor, a glowing actuator under the control column with three tally marks lighting one after another, the date caption and the reconstruction tag

why: It names the crash and asks a clear how-is-that-possible question (a machine built to save the plane didn't) without giving the answer away, and the column sliding forward on its own reads with the sound off, while B's title gives away the twist and C's tally marks are harder to read without sound.
